To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we constructed an antibody-enzyme fusion gene for the specific activation of an anticancer prodrug in B-cell lymphomas.
a single-chain anti CD20 mouse antibody and the human enzyme beta-glucuronase have been successfully fused to form a fusion protein.
a eukaryotically expressed fusion protein of a single-chain Fv fragment of anti-CD20 and human beta-gluaronidase can be used to target a prodrug to B-cell lymphoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the construction of a fusion protein consisting of the single-chain anti- CD20 mouse MoAb 1H4 linked to human beta-glucoseidase for the selective activation of anticancer agents at the tumor site in antibody-directed enzyme prodrugs therapy (ADEPT).
the construction of a fusion protein consisting of the single-chain anti- CD20 MoAb 1H4, and human beta-glucose-uridase.
the design and construction of a fusion protein that consists of a single-chain Fv antibody and human beta glucuronidase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has provided a basis for the future development of an anti-CD20-based ADEPT approach for the specific activation of prodrugs in lymphoma.
this is an excellent paper that will have a major impact in the field of ADEPT.
a fusion protein of a single-chain antibody and a human enzyme was constructed, and that the fusion protein was able to specifically activate a prodrug in a B-cell lymphoma cell line.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusion protein of a single-chain antibody and a human enzyme can be produced in a mammalian expression system and is a promising candidate for antibody-directed enzyme-prodrug therapy.
the fusion protein is an attractive candidate for future ADEPT trials.

the fusion protein is able to specifically bind to Daudi lymphoid cells, the fusion protein is capable of hydrolyzing the prodrug to the active drug and the fusion protein is cytotoxic to Daudi lymphocytes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the construction of a fusion protein between an antibody and an enzyme is technically feasible.
it is feasible to generate a eukaryotically expressed fusion protein of the anti-CD20 single-chain antibody and human beta-glu-curonidase for ADEPT.
we have constructed an anti-CD20 beta-glucuronase fusion protein that retains the enzymatic and immunological properties of the parental proteins.
